title: CAE reliability cliffs: orientation, discretization, and reference applicability
purpose: Turn common AI-to-CAE silent failures into deterministic verification obligations instead of treating successful execution as scientific acceptance.

execution.command: python -m pytest -q tests/test_verification.py tests/test_release_goldens.py -k 'rotation or convergence or inapplicable'
execution.evidence: A cantilever and its exactly rotated model must give the same response; convergence evidence requires an ordered discretization sequence; an inapplicable analytical theory produces an inconclusive claim rather than a false pass/fail.

observables: Maximum displacement before and after a 90-degree geometry/load/support rotation.
Finest-grid relative change and observed order from coarse-to-fine values.
Explicit applicability status for analytical or reduced-theory references.
Result trust state retained in campaign-to-learning provenance.
acceptance: The rotated isotropic cantilever satisfies the declared metamorphic tolerance.
A convergence claim cannot pass when required order evidence is unavailable.
An out-of-domain reference is inconclusive rather than accepted.
A training dataset can require verified evidence and reject merely computed cases.
limitations: Version 0.1 covers the section/load-axis failure class with a clean-room metamorphic case; it does not reproduce an unpublished third-party CalculiX deck.
The perforated-plate local-stress mesh-convergence family is a release-critical next item and needs an open mesh generator or versioned external fixture.
The T-stiffener theory-selection family requires explicit beam, shell, and 3D reference models before it can be advertised.
